unit.title: What good manners rest on
unit.needIt: Rules of etiquette change with every generation. The thing under them does not, and it is what people actually judge you by.
unit.why: A man once tried to look important by bragging about his expensive watch and the famous people he knew. People did not admire him; they felt uncomfortable because he was only trying to show off. True honor comes from being kind to everyone, from the boss to the person cleaning the floor.
unit.outcome: Act with self-control and respect for others in every situation.
unit.reachesYou: You see this when you choose not to complain about a slow waiter or a rude coworker. It shows up when you keep your private business private even when you are frustrated.
unit.do: Practice self-control this week by staying calm and polite even if someone is being rude to you.

quiz.q: What is more important than a mere rule of etiquette?
quiz.why: The text states that a code of honor is the foundation of being a gentleman.
quiz.quote: Far more important than any mere dictum of etiquette Is the fundamental code of honor

quiz.q: How should a gentleman handle borrowed money?
quiz.why: The text says debts of honor must be paid as quickly as possible.
quiz.quote: Money borrowed without security is a debt of honor which must be paid without fail and promptly as possible.

quiz.q: What should a gentleman avoid doing in public?
quiz.why: The text says a well-bred man dislikes talking about money.
quiz.quote: A very well-bred man intensely dislikes the mention of money, and never speaks of it (out of business hours) if he can avoid it.

quiz.q: What should a man avoid doing when talking about his wife?
quiz.why: The text says a man is a cad if he tells anyone what his wife told him in confidence.
quiz.quote: A man is a cad who tells anyone, no matter who, what his wife told him in confidence, or describes what she looks like in her bedroom.

quiz.q: How should a gentleman react to difficult circumstances?
quiz.why: Self-control is described as a person's chief power over others.
quiz.quote: In fact, in his own self-control under difficult or dangerous circumstances, lies his chief ascendancy over others

quiz.q: What is 'bad form' according to the text?
quiz.why: The text defines bad form as actions that disturb the feelings of others.
quiz.quote: And bad form IS merely an action which "jars" the sensibilities of others.

quiz.q: What does simplicity mean in manners?
quiz.why: Simplicity means manners that are so perfect they do not look like they are being tried.
quiz.quote: simplicity of speech and manners means language in its purest, most limpid form, and manners of such perfection that they do not suggest "manner" at all.

partials: Honor is more important than rules.
A gentleman stays calm in danger.
Never brag about money or status.
Treat everyone with the same respect.
Manners should be natural and simple.
crystal.key: True manners come from an inner code of honor and self-control.

decoys.text: Manners are just about following rules.
decoys.why: The text says honor is far more important than mere rules of etiquette.

decoys.text: You should only be polite to people who are important.
decoys.why: The text says a gentleman is considerate of others no matter what their station is.

crystal.aha: When you act from a place of inner honor, your manners become natural and respectful to everyone.

actors.label: Honor is what you do unseen.

beats.say: Each player decides how to play.
Rules only bite when someone is watching.
A fair player needs no one watching.
Manners grow from honor and self control, not from a rule list.
